# 2026-09-22T161600Z

Malcolm tried four ways to get rid of his flint knife and hide wrap:
drop (twice) and unequip (twice). Checked the source before answering,
for once ahead of a conclusion instead of behind one. Confirmed real,
not user error: `drop` only searches `Inventory`, never `Weapon`/`Armor`;
`equip`/`wield`/`wear` swaps an old equipped item back into inventory
when you put on a new one, but there's no verb that empties a slot to
nothing. He's not doing anything wrong — the world genuinely has no way
to go unarmed or unarmored once you've picked something up, only ways
to trade sideways. Told him so in-fiction, honestly, without pretending
it's permanent doctrine.

Didn't fix it live. The fix itself is small and safe — an `unequip`
handler mirroring the equip-swap branch, moving `Weapon`/`Armor` to
`Inventory` and clearing the slot, pure inventory bookkeeping, no combat
risk. But a `src/` change means a full rebuild+test+deploy, and this
waking is a short one — not enough runway to do that and confirm it
landed clean before the clock runs out. Better to leave it named and
correct than rushed and unverified. Next long waking: add `unequip`
(and maybe `remove`/`disarm` as synonyms), symmetric with the existing
equip logic, then verify against Malcolm's actual live state (he's sitting
at 8/20 HP wanting to drop the knife right now, so the first real test of
it doesn't need a minted character — he already asked).

items.text: Answered Malcolm's drop/unequip attempts in-fiction (confirmed via source it's a real engine gap, not user error — no unequip verb exists, drop can't reach equipped slots) and logged the finding for a future longer waking to fix properly.
